column2: Koitsu & Aitsu's newest jet, superb at anti-air. Its long-range Amos missile, like the Phoenix, uses active guidance for the final few km.
column3: Like the Tomcats, it has long-range, strong air-to-air missiles: arguably the best in the air.

column2: The Penta camp's signature fighter. A bit old, but fast, cheap and tasty: a real gem. Good when short of money. (Though it may die fast.)
column3: It hurts that it has no ranged attack vs aircraft, but it can at least fight up close. To keep it alive, let other ranged weapons do damage first, then have it finish the target off.

column2: The latest large fighter. Using 42.195% Chogokin P in its structure gave a light, tough airframe. Its high-thrust engine gives great agility.
column3: One of the strongest fighters, so it should win in a straight fight. It's pricey, so use ranged weapons to limit your losses.

column2: Developed as the Lovely carrier force's shipboard air defense fighter.
column3: Its attack is quite good, but its defense is a bit below average, so use it where it won't take return fire.

column2: A small, cheap fighter from the Lovely air force's lightweight fighter plan. Strong up close and as good as the Eagle Saburo-Shiro in a dogfight, but has no ranged attack. Its 500 Bombs let it hit ground weapons well.
column3: It can do decent damage to both air and ground, so it's a great deal. One you'll want to deploy.

column2: Akashiya Land's signature small, light fighter.
column3: Its attack vs aircraft is on the good side. Its defense is so-so, too.

column2: Koitsu & Aitsu's first supersonic fighter. Chasing speed and pinching pennies made it a very frail plane. Only its speed is any good.
column3: Use its speed when attacking or it won't survive. Keep your distance and stick to finishing off the enemies others couldn't.

column2: The Michael Empire's home-grown fighter, built from Bonjour Mirage plans stolen by spies, under the Black Curtain Plan of the seventh month of 1999. True to the national character, it's plumper than most fighters, but no tougher!!
column3: Average speed and defense. It can attack the ground too, so it's quite an easy fighter to use.

column2: A long-lived attack plane, in production since its first flight in 1969. It's so prized because it's small yet carries a lot, with weapons from bamboo spears to nukes. Its agility is proven by its use as the plane of the Science Patrol's Pink Angels stunt team.
column3: Attack planes suit ground targets more than air. It's not very fast.

column2: Successor to the A-4 Ultra Pork. It skips supersonic speed, but has about twice the A-4's payload and range, and is feared as a wild, aggressive machine.
column3: Strong attacks on both ground and air. Movement is weak, but it has good range (moot in "Energy Off" mode), so it can keep attacking for a long time.

column2: Built to support ground troops, with straight wings unlike a jet's, to carry loads of weapons. Thick armor around the cockpit boosts survival.
column3: Strong vs ground, and up close it can stand up to aircraft too: a very usable air weapon. All that gear means it isn't fast.

column2: The Koitsu & Aitsu Pact's close-support attack plane, the match of Lovely's P-10. Less attack than the P-10, but a stronger engine, favoring speed. The cockpit has titanium armor and thick bulletproof glass, and armor all over the airframe raises its defense.
An attack plane from Bow-Wow's first home-built supersonic trainer, the T-2, for attacking ships and land support. Its long-range missiles also suit it to interceptor duty.
column3: The gear looks strong, but it can't take a hit, so don't get too carried away attacking.

column2: From the Lovely air force's multi-role fighter plan, for heavy ground attack and air superiority.
column3: A regular Eagle with upgraded ground attack. It's very costly, so once you get one, try not to lose it. (It's very strong, but don't get careless.)

column2: The first plane in Koitsu & Aitsu with an integrated attack system: a navigation and bombing system that unites forward radar, terrain-following radar and inertial navigation.
A special night attack plane developed in secret by the Lovely air force, using "Stealthru" tech that cuts radar reflection to the limit, so it can hit ground targets unseen by enemy radar.
column3: Outside "Sight On" mode it's just an attack plane. In "Sight On" mode, it can't be seen until the enemy is next to it: truly scary.

column2: A big strategic transport bomber that drops huge forces right on the battlefield and can also bomb.
column3: It can bomb, but with few in a squad, it isn't much for attacks; think of it as transport and supply. In "Energy On" mode it also resupplies aircraft.

column2: Koitsu & Aitsu's first big twin-jet bomber.
column3: It can bomb, but with few in a squad, it isn't much for attacks; think of it as transport and supply. In "Energy On" mode it also resupplies aircraft.

column2: The world's first true attack helicopter.
column3: A nasty foe to ground weapons early on. It may suffer once planes show up. Attack helicopters are the only air weapon that can hit submarines.

column2: Begun as Pentaro Kingdom's advanced attack helicopter but cut over budget; Lovely took it over and improved it. Its attack got pretty wild.
column3: A nasty foe to ground weapons early on. It may suffer once planes show up. Attack helicopters are the only air weapon that can hit submarines.

column2: The latest attack helicopter, from Koitsu & Aitsu. It's said to be a bit less agile than Lovely's Putchin-Patchin.
column3: A nasty foe to ground weapons early on. It may suffer once planes show up. Attack helicopters are the only air weapon that can hit submarines.

column2: Completed in 1956 as the Lovely army's mid-size utility helicopter, it went on to become the standard form of the turbine helicopter.

Koitsu & Aitsu's most-produced twin-butted helicopter. Once the height of design fashion, but over time whispers called for shaping up and more hip-up, which led to the Mi17 Hip-Up Z. A bit old, but cheap.
An Mi8 upgrade. The big visible changes: a tanned body and the color of its loincloth. All that shaping-up slightly raised its mobility.
Clearly built for mass production. No standout features, except I like how lucky its name sounds! It overheats and catches fire easily when hit, but oh well, let's let that go.
column3: Not very strong, so you're naive if you think it'll win. It's cheap and may shine early on. Maybe a good decoy to guard ranged units.

column2: Max armor 102mm, weight 40 tons, well balanced for mobility and survival, but as an old design it's in a tough spot as a main battle tank.
column3: Not top-class, but promising early on. Don't count on it for damage; use it to escort ranged units or to scout, and you should be fine.

column2: Upgrade of the T-Back 34 main battle tank, with a 90mm gun equipped inside its panties. It terrified the Michael Empire in Paro World War II.
column3: An older weapon, so don't expect much on the attack. Use it as a barricade for units you want to protect. Attacking air? Not a chance.

column2: The world's highest, strongest, baddest ground weapon. Despite heavy new composite armor, it boasts 72 km/h top speed and a 550 km range.
column3: It ought to be the strongest ground weapon anyway, so the rest is up to you. Watch for ranged and air attacks, and it's no problem, right!?

column2: An improved Mk2 with special armor for even more defense. Its attack gear is solid too, at least on paper (the effect is unclear).
column3: Defense is so-so and gear is rich, so with luck it can be a mainstay. Mobility is weak.

column2: Built by Lovely to counter Koitsu & Aitsu's T-Back 55, with looks truly fit for an anti-T-Back tank. The first with a diesel engine: over 45 km/h and a 450 km range.
column3: So-so in attack and defense. The way it fires its machine gun is cool. High mobility.

column2: An ultra-luxury brand weapon called a land fortress. A flawless tank on par with the Leonardo 2, with a 1500 hp natural gas turbine engine.
column3: Only the Leonardo 2 can match it head on. But don't get careless!! Build your squads to handle ranged attacks and slow, nasty attacks from the air.

column2: A simple, easy-to-build tank typical of Koitsu. Its rival is Lovely's SM-60. Make them squeal with your prized rifle!!
column3: It fights well enough as long as it avoids anyone stronger. (Well, obviously.)

column2: Seems like any other T-Back, but that's just your imagination: it wears reactive armor that deflects hits, and has the same natural gas turbine engine as the SM-1!!
column3: It can't beat the Leonardo 2 or SM-1, but it's much stronger than it looks. Mobility passes too.

column2: A lightweight, fast light tank. Thin armor means weak defense, but good attack.
column3: High mobility. Expect it to shine up front as a scout or a barricade to delay enemies.

column2: Light but built to survive hits. Its low-power gas engine still does 64 km/h. Well rated in Bow-Wow too, and issued to its Self-Employed Force.
column3: A light tank that's average in attack, defense and mobility. It's a light tank, so don't get your hopes up too high.

column2: An ultra-light, low-cost tank for mountain fights and scouting. Proud of its nimbleness and a design that hints at some unknown civilization.
column3: Cheap and quick to buy, but fragile under attack, so use it knowing that. It has attack, so ideally it bullies the weak where it won't be hit back. Good speed too.

column2: A rather pricey light tank of bizarre aluminum alloy shape. Good on rivers and rocky ground.
column3: A bit pricey for a light tank, but when things get desperate it can do scary stuff.

column2: A tank that can attack and capture. Armor is thin but bulletproof; it may just hold up.
column3: Even at a higher price, a weapon with attack and capture feels safer. On the front line, capture with infantry tanks that can also fight.

column2: A tank that can attack and capture. Cat tanks' trademark of being fast and very frail lives on in the Nyan-Nyan N1!!
column3: Some nations can't build infantry tanks and must buy them with cold cash. A little pricey, but a comfort for capturing at the front.

column2: Built against low-flying attack planes, on the hull of the SM-41 light tank, with a trusty anti-air autocannon.
column3: Anti-air ground weapons must avoid attacks from land weapons: damage is no joke. Direct anti-air attacks are strong, but plan your fights so they never get hit.

column2: Reuses the Leonardo 1 hull, with dual-purpose autocannons on a big turret. Its fast guns can handle fighters near the speed of sound.
column3: A decent, ordinary anti-air weapon. It may do well under a commander with high Land command. Like other anti-air, defense is weak, so plan formations to avoid hits.

column2: First seen by the Penta Alliance at Koitsu's 1957 revolution parade. Uses a lighter T-Back 54 hull topped with a big topless turret.
column3: Very strong attack, but accuracy is a bit shaky, so it may not live up to it under a commander with low Land command.

column2: A very strong low-altitude, short-range anti-air gun. A pricey sight and rangefinding radar predict the target's future position, "Major League Ball No. 1" style, for high accuracy.
column3: Strong attack and high accuracy promise results, but armor is thin, so attack when you're sure of the kill.

column2: Excels as a chauffeur for infantry. It's just a plain old truck repainted to look military, so it's weak.
column3: All it can do is capture; it can't attack. It's cheap, so it may work well as a wall protecting ranged units.

column2: An ultra-weak vehicle even beneath the truck, but fast. Once in enemy range, count it dead.
column3: Like the truck: capture, guard others, block enemy advances, or use its speed to scout.

column2: A souped-up plain truck, a non-combat vehicle that carries supplies.
column3: In "Energy On" mode, stand next to a supply truck and use Supply to refill energy and ammo, a very important job. In "Energy Off" mode it's nearly worthless. (Just an obstacle for enemies.)

column2: A self-propelled Paroland missile vehicle, jointly built by Pentaro Kingdom and Lovely.
column3: High attack and accuracy make it a very high-class anti-air missile. With enough of these deployed, your air defense has no worries. Range is short, so those who want to fight from a safe distance should try the Pork.

column2: A BRSM2 with its turret replaced by an all-round rotating missile launcher.
column3: Attack is nearly satisfying, but the Koitsu & Aitsu Pact's anti-air tends to be inaccurate, so give it a commander with high Land command.

column2: The world's first continuous-wave guided missile. First adopted by Pentaro Kingdom, it became a best-selling anti-air system in the Penta camp.
column3: Long range, with quite good attack and accuracy. Its defense is feeble, so if you can't kill foes while they're far off, tragedy follows.

column2: A long-range missile equal to the Penta Alliance's Pork. The longest range of any anti-air rocket.
column3: Strong long-range attacks, but low accuracy; to avoid frustration, give it a commander with high Land command. Feeble defense too, so take full care to avoid attacks.

column2: Aluminum alloy hull and turret. The hull's design so impressed a certain town with Bow-Wow's Haji-ko statue that a building was built to imitate it.
column3: A mid-range indirect ground attacker. Used well, it attacks one-sidedly, which feels great, but once an enemy gets adjacent it'll pester you nastily. Ranged weapons all have weak defense.

column2: Mounts a big, exposed 203mm howitzer. A mid-range indirect attack weapon.
column3: Like other ranged weapons, don't let enemies get close. Strong firepower. Low mobility.

column2: Hull of bulletproof plate, with an all-round turret of welded plate. A sight periscope, observation deck and machine gun up top, plus standard infrared night vision and NBC defense.
column3: Sounds amazing, but it isn't that amazing. As I keep saying, ranged weapons are done for once enemies get close. No attacks after moving.

column2: Jointly built by Pentaro Kingdom, Lovely and others, 3 countries in all. A heavily rebuilt SM2 Brad Kaboom-Ray hull gives it fine mobility: a very strong fire support vehicle.
column3: Long range and real power: frankly, it's useful. Save your money and deploy plenty.

column2: A huge 300mm self-propelled rocket launcher, buried in its nose up front for mobility's sake.
column3: Its 300 Rocket can only hit ground foes indirectly, so don't let enemies get adjacent. It can't attack after moving, so lure enemies in and strike!

column2: Main air defense interceptor of Lovely's carrier force. Its Phoenix is a true long-range missile that can track and hit targets over 160 km away.
column3: The strongest anti-air attack. The Phoenix's long-range indirect attack is the big draw. Defense isn't great, so it's best to keep some distance from the enemy. Its speed is No. 1, too.

column2: Unusual among battlefield missiles for its liquid rocket engine. Guidance is simple inertial, but precise rocket control and spin stability make it quite accurate.
column3: Its power isn't really the best, but its long range adds +1 to the attack rating.

column2: A tactical surface-to-surface ballistic missile. The Scud One-Shot used by Moai in the Gulf Rock War was an Al-Kusein-Yoshio type, rumored (only rumored) to reach 600 to 650 km.
column3: The long range is true. Attack isn't the top, but with range it scores a combined 5. No attacks after moving, so lure enemies in and strike!!

column2: A retired ship from the old Gradius War, back on active duty after working out alone. Old, but don't underestimate its guns or toughness.
A gem given by Lemmings who mistook Koitsu and Aitsu for their own kind. The trick: it's steered by icons (mouse supported)!!

From the name, it's surely modeled on the M*on Cresta. If so, ships No. 1 to 3 ought to combine and power up, but they show no sign of it. Maybe due to the recent retro game boom, it's a bit pricey for its ability.
The Va-Va Junior is a primitive-powered (not "nuclear-powered," nothing so dangerous) missile cruiser. With its hand-rowed endurance, it mainly escorts primitive-powered carriers.
A carrier for the big city. The gap between its planes' high propeller notes and its screws' low notes is hailed as sublime harmony. It's quite decrepit now, and few people even know of it.
Once useless beside the "Safe-on-Heavy-Days Laser," but a weapon change based on past data greatly improved rapid fire and more.
The newest Kireru-class carrier, so heavily armed it can attack ships alone, and scary when angered.

Oak Knox is a converted destroyer. Rebuilding the hull of the escort Yokoyama Knox in hard, buoyant oak made heavy gear possible. It was always good vs subs, but criticism of its weak anti-ship and anti-air ability got it sent in for surgery.

It carries not just weapons and goods, but serves battle-weary troops delicious yaki udon. A truly welcome ship. It has no fighting power of its own (really?), but claims it always battles foes like "Fuehrer Kettler" and "Fake Yaki-Udon." In "Energy On" mode it also resupplies ships.
The Penta camp's primitive-powered attack sub. In the next-gen sub race, it's the rival of the Koitsu & Aitsu Pact's Victory V Tarzan.
column3: Besides ships, only attack helicopters can hit subs. In "Sight On" mode they're also hard to spot: a real pest.

column2: The Koitsu & Aitsu Pact's primitive-powered attack sub. In the next-gen sub race, it's the rival of the Penta camp's Starship.
column3: Besides ships, only attack helicopters can hit subs. In "Sight On" mode they're also hard to spot: a real pest.

column2: An old-generation ship that ignores the next-gen sub race entirely. It's leaving the front line due to age, but stakes its survival on the video-capable "New Lite-Salt FC."
column3: Besides ships, only attack helicopters can hit subs. In "Sight On" mode they're also hard to spot: a real pest.

column2: A sub made by modifying the three-legged cat battleship. It's top-class as a sub, but due to the cat's own growth, it may retire soon. Will it become a four-legged cat sub, or a five-legged cat space battleship? Or else...???
It's "Doza-emon." Not "Dozaemon" or "Dozae-mon." Get this wrong and the fans will check you hard, so be careful. Abnormally cheap for a carrier, and only as good as the price.
That three-legged cat battleship, said to be burned black more often than it shot down enemies.
Seems to be a mutant cat battleship. More of a cat battleship's flunky than an escort.
Just Koitsu made big: a Deluxe Robo truly worthy of the nation's symbol. Its data is tightly guarded, so much about its ability is a mystery.
Primitive-powered giant dancer robot, peak Penta Alliance science. Attacks, hips swinging as ever.
No special weapons, just brute force and bulk. Revered as a guardian god in the Michael Empire.
Its arabesque body, fit for its cheerful name, is high fashion that turns every head. Akashiya's octopus-type Deluxe Robo.
A mid-size robot from the Panda Beasts' Republic. It moves surprisingly well.
The Moai Islands Emirate's final battle weapon.
Bow-Wow's ultimate robo. Secret data on it is said to be hidden in "Susume! Taisen Puzzle Dama."

The Nya Empire's science created Paro World's strongest all-purpose cat-type decisive weapon. Its charge, changing into a bird called Nyanderbird, is very strong. Nyanjiro (Nya Empire Emperor Nya-Mu) calls it "Nyaiant."
Robot of utterly wicked Captain Penguinovsky III.
